questions.question: Under which classification does flame-resistant finish come? / a). Basic/routine finish b). Functional finish c). Aesthetic Finishes d). Colouration finish
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: Functional finish
  • Chemicals (resins) are applied to the fabric, primarily to cotton.
  • Special Calendering (Luster/Pattern Finishes): These finishes primarily change
  • the way light reflects off the fabric's surface, adding shine, gloss, or a specific
  • visual pattern.
  • o Examples include Schreinerizing (adds subtle luster) and Moiré (creates a
  • wavy, water-like pattern on ribbed fabrics).
  • o Embossing also falls here by pressing a three-dimensional pattern into the
  • surface.
  • Engraving: Large copper rollers are etched with the pattern and coated with
  • chromium. The size of the design determines the roller diameter.
questions.final_answer: chromium. The size of the design determines the roller diameter
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Why is shrinkage resistant finishing important for wool fabrics?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: Shrinkage resistant finishing is important for wool fabrics because they can suffer
  • from felting shrinkage, which occurs when the scales on wool fibers interlock due
  • to moisture, heat, and movement during washing, leading to a permanent reduction in
  • size.

questions.question: What is an advantage of yarn dyeing?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: The main advantage of yarn dyeing is that it allows for the creation of intricate
  • multicolored patterns (like plaids, stripes, checks, or Ikat) that are woven directly into
  • the fabric. This method ensures deep, uniform color penetration within the yarns
  • which results in patterns that are more durable and colorfast compared to designs
  • simply printed onto the finished fabric surface.
questions.final_answer: simply printed onto the finished fabric surface
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Why is sublimation printing not suitable for untreated cotton?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: Sublimation printing is not suitable for untreated cotton because the high
  • heat causes the special dyes to turn into a gas, and this gaseous dye can only bond
  • effectively with synthetic fibers like polyester, meaning the color will not stick
  • permanently to cotton.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the embossing process in textile finishing?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: The embossing process involves passing the fabric between two rollers: a
  • metal roller with a raised design and a soft roller (made of cloth or paper). The metal
  • roller presses the design into the soft roller, and when the fabric passes between them
  • it picks up the raised design, creating a visible, three-dimensional texture and pattern
  • on its surface.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

  • garments are dipped into a dye bath either partially or completely to create gradient

  • intensity and coverage of the colour over different sections of the item, which is
  • necessary to achieve the desired gradient or ombré effect.

• In functional finishes, explain how water-repellent finishes improve the
  • comfort and utility of fabrics.
  • Ans: Water-repellent finishes improve comfort by preventing the fabric from
  • getting soaked (keeping the wearer dry) while still allowing air to pass through
  • (making it breathable). They improve utility by making the fabric resist getting
  • wet so it can be used for items like outdoor or sports clothing that need to
  • stay dry for long periods.

questions.question: Why is shrinkage resistant finishing important for wool fabrics?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: Shrinkage resistant finishing is important for wool fabrics because they can suffer
  • from felting shrinkage, which occurs when the scales on wool fibers interlock due
  • to moisture, heat, and movement during washing, leading to a permanent reduction in
  • size.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: What is an advantage of yarn dyeing?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: The main advantage of yarn dyeing is that it allows for the creation of intricate
  • multicolored patterns (like plaids, stripes, checks, or Ikat) that are woven directly into
  • the fabric. This method ensures deep, uniform color penetration within the yarns
  • which results in patterns that are more durable and colorfast compared to designs
  • simply printed onto the finished fabric surface.
questions.final_answer: simply printed onto the finished fabric surface
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Why is sublimation printing not suitable for untreated cotton?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: Sublimation printing is not suitable for untreated cotton because the high
  • heat causes the special dyes to turn into a gas, and this gaseous dye can only bond
  • effectively with synthetic fibers like polyester, meaning the color will not stick
  • permanently to cotton.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the embossing process in textile finishing?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: The embossing process involves passing the fabric between two rollers: a
  • metal roller with a raised design and a soft roller (made of cloth or paper). The metal
  • roller presses the design into the soft roller, and when the fabric passes between them
  • it picks up the raised design, creating a visible, three-dimensional texture and pattern
  • on its surface.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: What is dip dyeing, and why are fabrics dipped repeatedly?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: What is dip dyeing? Dip dyeing is a manual technique where fabric, yarn, or
  • garments are dipped into a dye bath either partially or completely to create gradient
  • ombré, or two-tone effects.
  • Why are fabrics dipped repeatedly? Fabrics are dipped repeatedly to control the
  • intensity and coverage of the colour over different sections of the item, which is
  • necessary to achieve the desired gradient or ombré effect.
questions.final_answer: necessary to achieve the desired gradient or ombré effect
